title: Affine Lie Algebras and Loop Central Extensions

items.title: Loop algebra of a simple Lie algebra
items.statement: For a nonzero finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra g, its algebraic loop algebra is Lg=g tensor_C C[t,t^-1], with [x tensor f,y tensor q]=[x,y] tensor fq. Only Laurent polynomials occur; no topology, completion, smooth-loop space, or analytic loop group is intended.
items.strategy: Extend the finite Lie bracket and Laurent multiplication bilinearly. Antisymmetry and Jacobi reduce termwise to the corresponding identities in g, and every sum is finite.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Section 7.1
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Section 12.2.1

items.title: Residue two cocycle on a loop algebra
items.statement: Fix the rescaling of the Killing form whose induced finite-root form gives every long root squared length two. Define omega(x tensor f,y tensor q)=(x,y) Res(f' q dt), extended bilinearly. For modes x_m=x tensor t^m, omega(x_m,y_n)=m delta_{m,-n}(x,y). For every long root alpha, opposite root vectors normalized by [e_alpha,f_alpha]=alpha^vee satisfy (e_alpha,f_alpha)=1.
items.strategy: The Killing form is invariant and nondegenerate on simple g and has a unique positive-real rescaling giving long roots squared length two. The residue formula on monomials gives m delta_{m,-n}; prove alternatingness from the zero residue of (fq)' and the cyclic cocycle identity from the zero residue of 2(fqh)' before using the central extension.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Sections 7.1-7.2
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Lemma 12.2.5

items.title: The loop residue form is alternating
items.statement: For all u,v in Lg, omega(u,v)=-omega(v,u); in particular omega(u,u)=0.
items.strategy: For Laurent polynomials f,q, the coefficient of t^-1 in (fq)' is zero, so Res(f'q dt)+Res(fq' dt)=0. Symmetry of the invariant form gives the alternating identity on pure tensors, and bilinearity gives it in general.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, equations (7.1)-(7.2)
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Lemma 12.2.5

items.title: The loop residue form satisfies the Lie two cocycle identity
items.statement: For all u,v,w in Lg, omega([u,v],w)+omega([v,w],u)+omega([w,u],v)=0.
items.strategy: On x tensor f,y tensor q,z tensor r, invariance and symmetry identify all three Lie-form coefficients with ([x,y],z). The remaining scalar is Res((fq)'r+(qr)'f+(rf)'q)dt=2 Res((fqr)'dt)=0. Extend trilinearly.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Section 7.1
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Lemma 12.2.5 and Corollary 12.2.6

items.title: Untwisted affine central extension
items.statement: The untwisted central extension is Lg bar=Lg direct-sum Cc, where c is central and [u+ac,v+bc]=[u,v]_L+omega(u,v)c. Equivalently [x_m,y_n]=[x,y]_{m+n}+m delta_{m,-n}(x,y)c.
items.strategy: Alternatingness gives an alternating bracket and the two-cocycle identity is exactly the central component of Jacobi; the loop component satisfies Jacobi by the loop-algebra definition.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Section 7.1
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Definition 12.2.3 and Corollary 12.2.6

items.title: Degree derivation and full untwisted affine algebra
items.statement: The degree derivation d acts by [d,x_m]=m x_m and [d,c]=0. The full untwisted affine algebra is g hat=Lg direct-sum Cc direct-sum Cd with the central-extension bracket and this semidirect derivation action.
items.strategy: The operator t d/dt is a derivation of Laurent polynomials and preserves the residue cocycle because the cocycle term can be nonzero only when the two mode degrees sum to zero. Thus it is a derivation of the central extension and the semidirect bracket satisfies Jacobi.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Sections 7.1-7.2
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Definition 12.2.3 and Fact 12.2.7

items.title: The derived affine algebra omits only the degree derivation
items.statement: For nonzero finite-dimensional simple g, [g hat,g hat]=Lg direct-sum Cc. Thus the full affine algebra is not perfect, while its derived algebra is precisely the one-dimensional central extension of the loop algebra.
items.strategy: Simplicity makes g perfect, so each x_m is [y_m,z_0] for a finite sum of brackets. Nondegeneracy supplies x,y with (x,y)=1; [x_1,y_-1]=[x,y]_0+c and the loop term is already derived, so c is derived. Every bracket has zero d-coordinate, giving the reverse inclusion.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Sections 7.1-7.2
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Section 12.2.1

items.title: Null root, central coroot, and affine level
items.statement: For h hat=h direct-sum Cc direct-sum Cd, extend every finite root by zero on c and d. Define delta in h hat* by delta(h direct-sum Cc)=0 and delta(d)=1. The central element c is the affine central coroot, and the level of a weight Lambda is Lambda(c). This is the loop normalization fixed by the normalized invariant form.
items.strategy: The direct-sum Cartan makes the extensions and delta unique. Centrality of c makes Lambda(c) constant along a cyclic weight module; the later loop/GCM comparison identifies this c with the primitive affine central coroot in the stated normalization.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Section 7.2
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Section 12.2.2

items.title: The affine simple root alpha zero is delta minus the highest root
items.statement: Let theta be the unique highest root of the irreducible finite root system of g. With the invariant form normalized by (theta,theta)=2, put alpha_0=delta-theta and h_0=c-theta^vee. Together with the finite simple roots and coroots these are independent realization data for the untwisted affine GCM, and normalized root vectors satisfy [f_theta tensor t,e_theta tensor t^-1]=h_0.
items.strategy: The adjoint g-module is simple because g is simple, so the finite highest-weight construction gives it a unique dominant highest weight; its weights are the finite roots together with zero, hence this highest weight is the unique highest root theta. Normalize e_theta,f_theta so [e_theta,f_theta]=theta^vee and (e_theta,f_theta)=1. The mode bracket then gives c-theta^vee. Direct pairings with alpha_0 and h_0 give the untwisted affine Cartan entries, independence follows from the d- and c-coordinates, and the invariant form symmetrizes the matrix.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Sections 6.3 and 7.2
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Sections 12.1-12.2.2

items.proof_strategy: finite root strings and direct computation

items.title: Loop and affine GCM presentations are isomorphic
items.statement: Let A hat be the untwisted affine GCM constructed from the finite simple g. The assignment e_0 to f_theta tensor t, f_0 to e_theta tensor t^-1, h_0 to c-theta^vee, and the remaining Chevalley and Cartan generators to their degree-zero loop copies extends uniquely to an isomorphism g(A hat) isomorphic to g hat, fixing h hat.
items.strategy: Check the Cartan, mixed, and Serre relations using alpha_0=delta-theta, the highest-root strings, and the normalized mode bracket. The Serre presentation gives a homomorphism. Its kernel is Cartan-disjoint because the map fixes h hat, hence is zero by the defining maximal-ideal property of g(A hat). Degree zero generates g; simplicity makes the degree-one root vector generate g as an adjoint g-module, and induction on positive and negative modes proves surjectivity, with c and d already in the Cartan.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Theorem 7.2.1
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Theorem 12.2.15

items.title: Affine Weyl group is a coroot lattice semidirect product
items.statement: The untwisted affine Weyl group is the semidirect product of the finite Weyl group W_0 and the translation subgroup indexed by the finite coroot lattice Q^vee. Every element has a unique form t_gamma w, and with the normalized invariant form B its action is t_gamma(lambda)=lambda+lambda(c)nu(gamma)-(lambda(gamma)+B(gamma,gamma)lambda(c)/2)delta; also t_gamma t_eta=t_(gamma+eta) and w t_gamma w^-1=t_(w gamma).
items.strategy: Use the normalized invariant form to verify the displayed translation action, addition, and conjugation directly. Compute s_0=t_(theta^vee)s_theta. Finite root strings show the W_0-orbit of the highest coroot generates Q^vee, so all translations lie in W_aff and the simple reflections generate no more. Translation/finite intersection is trivial by their affine action, giving uniqueness.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Section 6.4
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Theorem 12.2.19 and Lemma 12.2.20

items.title: Roots of an untwisted affine Lie algebra
items.statement: Relative to h hat, the roots of the untwisted affine algebra are alpha+n delta for alpha in the finite root system and n in Z, together with n delta for nonzero n. The alpha+n delta roots are real with multiplicity one; the n delta roots are imaginary with multiplicity rank(g). The corresponding spaces are g_alpha tensor t^n and h tensor t^n.
items.strategy: Compute all Cartan weights and multiplicities directly. Use the positive semidefinite root form and simple-reflection positive-height descent to prove every positive-norm root is real; isotropic nonzero delta multiples cannot be in a simple-root orbit. This avoids an implicit arithmetic orbit-classification lemma.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Section 7.2 and Corollary 7.2.2
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Proposition 12.2.14 and Corollary 12.2.16

items.title: Evaluation module at a nonzero loop parameter
items.statement: For a nonzero a in C and a finite-dimensional g-module (V,rho), evaluation ev_a(x tensor f)=f(a)x is a Lie homomorphism Lg to g. Its pullback makes V an Lg-module; extending by c acting as zero makes it a level-zero module for the central extension Lg bar.
items.strategy: Multiplicativity of Laurent-polynomial evaluation proves ev_a preserves brackets. The central-extension relation is respected after c acts by zero because the image bracket is exactly f(a)q(a)rho([x,y]); nonzero a is required for negative powers.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Section 7.1 loop-algebra conventions
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Section 12.2.1 loop-algebra conventions

items.title: Evaluation modules have level zero and do not extend canonically over d
items.statement: Every evaluation module has c acting zero. If its finite Lie action is nonzero it admits no compatible d action. If that action is zero, every endomorphism D is compatible; D=0 is a natural choice, but the relations do not force it when V is nonzero. On V=0 the zero endomorphism is unique. Thus evaluation does not in general extend to the full affine algebra.
items.strategy: Compare the m=0 and m=1 commutator relations for nonzero finite action. For zero finite action every D satisfies every relation; if V is nonzero D=0 and D=id are distinct, whereas End(0) has one member. The literal no-canonical-choice scaffold phrase is replaced by this precise operator classification.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Sections 7.1-7.2
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Definition 12.2.3

items.title: Twisted loop algebra from a diagram automorphism
items.statement: Let sigma be a finite-order diagram automorphism of g of order r, let zeta be a primitive r-th root of unity, and write g_j for its zeta^j-eigenspace. The twisted loop algebra is the fixed algebra of tau(x tensor t^m)=zeta^-m sigma(x) tensor t^m, equivalently the direct sum over m in Z of g_(m mod r) tensor t^m. The same fixed-point construction inside g hat retains c and d. No classification of twisted affine types is asserted here.
items.strategy: The diagram automorphism preserves the normalized invariant form, so tau preserves the loop bracket, residue central term, c, and d. Fixed points of a Lie automorphism form a Lie subalgebra. Finite-order eigenspace decomposition gives the displayed congruence description.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Section 8.2
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Definition 14.1.2 and Proposition 14.1.3

title: Affine Lie Algebras and Loop Central Extensions — Examples

items.title: Affine sl2 mode brackets
items.statement: For sl2 with (e,f)=1 and (h,h)=2, the affine mode relations are [e_m,f_n]=h_(m+n)+m delta_(m,-n)c, [h_m,h_n]=2m delta_(m,-n)c, and [d,e_m]=m e_m.
items.strategy: Insert the three finite sl2 brackets and normalized form values into the mode formula, including the cases m+n=0 and m=0, and compute the d-bracket from the degree definition.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Sections 7.1-7.2
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Definition 12.2.3

items.title: The Heisenberg subalgebra of an affine Lie algebra
items.statement: The subspace Cc direct-sum over nonzero m of h tensor t^m is a Heisenberg Lie algebra: [h tensor t^m,k tensor t^n]=m delta_(m,-n)(h,k)c, and c is its one-dimensional center. The zero Cartan modes are deliberately excluded.
items.strategy: Finite Cartan elements commute, so the loop component vanishes and only the residue term remains. Nondegeneracy pairs each nonzero mode with its opposite; hence no nonzero mode is central, while c is central by construction.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Section 7.2
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Proposition 12.2.14

items.title: The affine A1 simple roots and GCM
items.statement: For finite sl2 with root alpha and coroot h, theta=alpha and alpha_0=delta-alpha, h_0=c-h. The pairings of alpha_0,alpha_1 with h_0,h_1 give the affine A1 GCM [[2,-2],[-2,2]], including its two double-edge off-diagonal entries.
items.strategy: Use alpha(h)=2, delta(h_0)=delta(h_1)=0, alpha(c)=0, and alpha_0=delta-alpha to compute all four pairings explicitly; then identify the loop generators e_0=f tensor t and f_0=e tensor t^-1.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Sections 6.1 and 7.2
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Proposition 12.2.13

items.title: An evaluation module for affine sl2
items.statement: On the two-dimensional standard sl2-module and for a nonzero a, define (x tensor t^m)v=a^m x v and cv=0. This is a level-zero module for the derived affine algebra, but it has no compatible degree-derivation action.
items.strategy: Write the standard e,f,h matrices, check the mode bracket after applying a^(m+n), and note that the central term acts as zero. Apply the m=0 versus m=1 commutator contradiction to any proposed d-operator.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Sections 7.1-7.2
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Definition 12.2.3

items.title: Omitting the central term breaks the affine GCM bracket
items.statement: In the unextended loop algebra, the affine candidates e_0=f_theta tensor t and f_0=e_theta tensor t^-1 satisfy [e_0,f_0]=-theta^vee rather than h_0=c-theta^vee. Thus deleting the residue term does not realize the untwisted affine GCM presentation.
items.strategy: Compute the bracket once in the ordinary loop algebra and once in the central extension. The missing c-coordinate cannot be repaired inside the unextended loop algebra because its Cartan is only the finite Cartan plus d.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, equations (7.3)-(7.5)
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Theorem 12.2.15

items.title: The residue cocycle depends on invariant form normalization
items.statement: The numerical cocycle and level normalization are not intrinsic before the invariant form is fixed. Replacing ( , ) by a( , ) multiplies omega by a; the isomorphism to the original extension sends the new central generator c_a to a^-1 c, so transported numerical levels scale by a^-1.
items.strategy: Evaluate both cocycles on x tensor t and y tensor t^-1 with (x,y) nonzero. Compare the two brackets and solve for the central-generator image required by a Lie isomorphism fixing every loop mode; then evaluate a transported weight on that generator.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Sections 7.1-7.2
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Sections 12.1-12.2

items.title: Kac Moody formal character completion
items.statement: For a finite generalized Cartan matrix, let E be the complex vector space of formal sums sum_mu c_mu e^mu whose support is contained in a finite union of downward cones lambda_j-Q^+. Define e^lambda e^mu=e^(lambda+mu), coefficientwise addition, and ch V=sum_mu dim(V_mu)e^mu for V in category O. Every coefficient of a product is a finite sum.
items.strategy: For fixed cone tops and output weight, nonnegative simple-root coordinates of a decomposition have bounded height, hence only finitely many decompositions occur. Category O supplies finite weight spaces and the required support. This completion is formal, not analytic.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Section 9.2
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Section 10.7

items.title: Kac Moody Weyl vector
items.statement: A Weyl vector is rho in h* with rho(h_i)=1 for every simple coroot. It exists but need not be unique when the simple coroots do not span h; shifted formulas are unchanged by a Weyl-invariant difference.
items.strategy: Prescribe value one on the span of the independent simple coroots and extend over a finite-dimensional complement. The difference of two choices vanishes on all h_i and is fixed by every simple reflection.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Sections 2.3 and 10.1
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras, Chapter 11

items.title: Kac Moody denominator product with root multiplicities
items.statement: For symmetrizable A define D=e^rho product_{alpha in Delta^+}(1-e^-alpha)^(mult alpha) in E, where mult alpha=dim g_alpha. The normalized product e^-rho D has constant coefficient one. Imaginary-root factors retain their actual multiplicities.
items.strategy: At a fixed beta in Q^+, only positive-root degrees of height at most ht(beta) contribute, and each root space is finite dimensional. Thus each coefficient is a finite integer sum and the constant term is one.

references.title: Kleshchev, Sections 9.2 and 10.2
Perrin, Sections 10.7 and 11.2

items.title: The Kac Moody denominator is Weyl skew
items.statement: For each simple reflection s_i, s_i(D)=-D as a transformed formal product; hence w(D)=epsilon(w)D. This does not assert a global Weyl action on every downward-cone series.
items.strategy: The reflection permutes Delta^+ minus {alpha_i}, preserving multiplicities, and sends alpha_i to -alpha_i. Combine s_i(rho)=rho-alpha_i with the transformed alpha_i factor to get one minus sign. All coefficient rearrangements are finite.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lemma 10.1.1 and Section 10.2
Perrin, Section 11.2

items.title: Casimir constrained Verma character expansion
items.statement: If V is a symmetrizable Kac-Moody highest-weight module of highest weight Lambda in O, then coefficientwise locally finitely ch V=sum_mu c_mu ch M(mu), with integers c_mu, c_Lambda=1, and c_mu nonzero only if mu<=Lambda and ||mu+rho||^2=||Lambda+rho||^2.
items.strategy: Use finite truncations above each requested weight to obtain the locally finite simple-character expansion. Expand Vermas unitriangularly in simple characters and invert the locally finite system. A simple factor below a primitive vector of weight mu is a quotient of M(mu), so the central Casimir forces equality of shifted norms. Inversion preserves each norm block and the top coefficient.

references.title: Kleshchev, Proposition 9.2.5
Perrin, Lemma 11.2.4

items.title: The denominator quotient has only imaginary cone support
items.statement: Let A_rho=sum_w epsilon(w)e^(w rho). Its normalization has constant term one and is invertible. For C=D/A_rho, the quotient is Weyl invariant and every exponent e^-beta in its normalized support has beta in K^+={gamma in Q^+:w gamma in Q^+ for every w}. If its nonconstant support is nonempty, a least-height beta in that support satisfies beta(h_i)<=0 for every i. This does not identify K^+ with the imaginary roots.
items.strategy: Reduced-word inversion sets make the alternant coefficientwise locally finite. The denominator definition supplies the simple-axis slice P=1-e^-alpha_i, while the reflection formula gives the same slice for the normalized alternant. Recursively divide the transverse polynomial slices. Skew divided by skew is invariant; comparison with every Weyl translate forces support into the intersection of all w^-1 Q^+. A minimal-height support term and its simple reflection give beta(h_i)<=0 without relying on cancellation.

references.title: Kleshchev, Sections 5.3 and 10.1-10.2
Perrin, Section 11.2

items.title: Casimir norm excludes nonzero denominator corrections
items.statement: The quotient C has no nonzero beta in its normalized support, and therefore C=1. The exclusion uses the invariant form and Casimir constraint, not a claim that every beta in K^+ is a root.
items.strategy: Apply the constrained Verma expansion to the trivial module and multiply by the inverse Verma product, so every surviving e^(rho-beta) in D obeys ||rho-beta||^2=||rho||^2. Choose a least-height nonzero beta in C. No normalized-alternant term can occur at this same beta: such a term is rho-w rho, so it already satisfies the norm equality, while beta in K^+ and least-height invariance give beta^2<=0<2(rho,beta), a contradiction. All mixed product terms use smaller nonzero support of C and vanish by minimality. Hence the D coefficient is the nonzero C coefficient and must satisfy the norm equality, giving the same contradiction.

references.title: Kleshchev, Proposition 9.2.5 and Theorem 10.2.1
Perrin, Lemmas 11.2.4–11.2.5 and Theorem 11.2.1

items.title: Kac Moody denominator identity
items.statement: For symmetrizable A, e^rho product_{alpha in Delta^+}(1-e^-alpha)^(mult alpha)=sum_w epsilon(w)e^(w rho) in the formal downward-cone completion. Both sides are coefficientwise locally finite.
items.strategy: The quotient lemma constructs C=D/A_rho and the norm lemma proves C=1. Multiply by the normalized alternant. Retain actual root multiplicities and formal local finiteness.

references.title: Kleshchev, Theorem 10.2.1 at Lambda=0
Perrin, Theorem 11.2.1 at lambda=0

items.title: The shifted integrable character numerator is Weyl skew
items.statement: For dominant integral Lambda, D ch L(Lambda) is Weyl skew in the formal completion. The weight-space invariance used here is proved by explicit finite rank-one operators and is choice-free.
items.strategy: First place L(Lambda) in category O as the quotient of its Verma module. For each simple-root sl2, local nilpotence makes exp(e_i)exp(-f_i)exp(e_i) finite on each vector. This invertible operator maps V_mu to V_(s_i mu), proving character invariance without basis choices. Combine with denominator skewness. Do not use the inherited weight-invariance item whose broad statement declares AC.

references.title: Kleshchev, Section 10.1
Perrin, Section 11.2

items.title: Only the highest dot orbit can occur in the integrable numerator
items.statement: In the constrained Verma expansion for L(Lambda), skewness forces every nonzero coefficient onto w(Lambda+rho)-rho with coefficient epsilon(w); no extra dominant or imaginary-cone correction occurs.
items.strategy: Use reduced-word descent to move a regular shifted weight to the dominant chamber; singular weights have zero skew coefficient. If a distinct dominant mu+rho=Lambda+rho-beta occurs with beta=sum k_i alpha_i in Q^+, then both Lambda+rho and mu+rho are strictly dominant. Thus (beta,Lambda+mu+2rho)=sum_i k_i d_i((Lambda+rho)(h_i)+(mu+rho)(h_i)) is strictly positive, contradicting equality of their squared norms. Hence beta=0, and skewness determines the orbit signs.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lemma 10.1.2 and Theorem 10.2.1
Perrin, Lemma 11.2.5 and Theorem 11.2.1

items.title: Weyl Kac character formula
items.statement: For symmetrizable A and dominant integral Lambda, D ch L(Lambda)=sum_w epsilon(w)e^(w(Lambda+rho)); equivalently ch L(Lambda) is the shifted alternant divided by product_{alpha>0}(1-e^-alpha)^(mult alpha), in the formal completion.
items.strategy: Identify the numerator by the preceding lemma, then divide by the normalized denominator with constant term one. Preserve symmetrizability, dominant integrality, actual root multiplicities, and formal rather than analytic meaning.

references.title: Kleshchev, Theorem 10.2.1
Perrin, Theorem 11.2.1

items.title: Generalized Kostant partition function
items.statement: Define K(beta) by product_{alpha>0}(1-e^-alpha)^(-mult alpha)=sum_{beta in Q^+}K(beta)e^-beta and set K(gamma)=0 outside Q^+. Imaginary roots occur with mult alpha colors; K(0)=1 and every value is finite.
items.strategy: Use binomial series factorwise and the denominator height bound. Equivalently K(beta) counts finite colored multisets of positive roots totaling beta, with mult alpha colors.

references.title: Kleshchev, Corollary 10.2.2
Perrin, Section 11.2

items.title: Kac Moody Kostant multiplicity formula
items.statement: For every weight mu, dim L(Lambda)_mu=sum_w epsilon(w)K(w(Lambda+rho)-(mu+rho)); only finitely many terms are nonzero.
items.strategy: Expand the inverse denominator and compare the e^mu coefficient. Reduced-word height growth and the fixed cone make the contributing Weyl elements finite.

references.title: Kleshchev, Corollary 10.2.2
Perrin, Section 11.2

items.title: Weyl Kac specializes to the finite Weyl character formula
items.statement: For finite-type A, all positive roots are real of multiplicity one and the Weyl group and root set are finite, so Weyl-Kac is the ordinary Weyl character formula for the corresponding complex semisimple Lie algebra.
items.strategy: Substitute the finite-type root data and the semisimple identification into the formula; every sum and product becomes finite and follows the positive-Borel convention.

references.title: Kleshchev, Theorem 10.2.1 and finite-type discussion
Perrin, Theorem 11.2.1

items.title: Affine denominator separates real and imaginary root factors
items.statement: For an untwisted affine algebra from a finite root system Phi_0 of rank ell, the denominator product splits over real roots alpha+n delta and -alpha+(n+1)delta, each with multiplicity one, and imaginary roots n delta with multiplicity ell.
items.strategy: Use the explicit untwisted affine root list and multiplicities, and derive its positive-root split from delta=alpha_0+theta, the highest-root bound theta-beta in Q_+, and the finite one-sign convention. Partition the product and reindex the negative finite roots. Keep the n=0 real-positive family separate from the n>=1 negative-finite-root family so no factor is lost or duplicated.

references.title: Kleshchev, Sections 6.1-6.3 and 10.3
Perrin, Chapter 12

items.title: Weyl Kac products are formal not analytic identities here
items.statement: Every infinite sum, product, quotient and coefficient extraction on this page is in the formal downward-cone completion. No complex evaluation, analytic convergence, or rearrangement of a conditionally convergent series is asserted.
items.strategy: Collect the established coefficientwise-finiteness clauses. Equality means equality of formal coefficients, each determined by a finite computation; analytic specializations remain out of scope.

references.title: Kleshchev, Sections 9.2 and 10.2
Perrin, Sections 10.7 and 11.2

title: The Weyl Kac Character Formula — Examples

items.title: Finite A1 specialization of Weyl Kac
items.statement: For A=(2) and dominant m omega, Weyl-Kac becomes (e^((m+1)omega)-e^(-(m+1)omega))/(e^omega-e^-omega)=sum_{j=0}^m e^((m-2j)omega), the character of the (m+1)-dimensional simple sl2-module.
items.strategy: Use alpha=2omega, rho=omega, and W={1,s}. Cancel the finite geometric difference formally and list the weights, including m=0.

references.title: Kleshchev, Theorem 10.2.1 specialized to A1
Perrin, Theorem 11.2.1 specialized to A1

items.title: Real and imaginary factors in the affine sl2 denominator
items.statement: For untwisted affine sl2, with q=e^-delta and z=e^-alpha, the positive-root product is product_{n>=1}(1-q^n) product_{n>=0}(1-zq^n) product_{n>=1}(1-z^-1q^n); the first factor is imaginary and the others real.
items.strategy: Set ell=1 and Phi_0^+={alpha}; translate the three root families, preserving the distinct index starts. This is formal, not analytic Jacobi convergence.

references.title: Kleshchev, Section 10.3
Perrin, Section 12.3

items.title: First weight layers of the basic affine sl2 character
items.statement: For the basic level-one module L(Lambda_0) of untwisted affine sl2, put q=e^-delta and z=e^-alpha. Then e^-Lambda_0 ch L(Lambda_0)=1+(z^-1+1+z)q+(z^-1+2+z)q^2+terms of delta-degree at least three, coefficientwise in the formal completion.
items.strategy: Insert the explicit level-three shifted affine Weyl translations into the alternating numerator, truncate to (1-z)+(z^3-z^-2)q^2, and divide by the real/imaginary product whose first terms are (1-z)(1-(1+z+z^-1)q+0q^2). Compute each resulting coefficient through degree two directly; no unproved theta-product identity is used.

references.title: Kleshchev, Sections 6.4 and 11.2
Perrin, Chapter 12

items.title: Using multiplicity one for imaginary roots gives the wrong affine denominator
items.statement: In untwisted affine type A2, delta has multiplicity two. Replacing every imaginary-root multiplicity by one changes (1-e^-delta)^2 to (1-e^-delta), so the normalized denominator already has the wrong e^-delta coefficient.
items.strategy: Use the A-page affine loop-root classification, whose delta root space is h_0 tensor t of dimension rank(sl3)=2. The direct delta-factor contribution changes from -2 to -1 while all other factor contributions agree, giving a formal coefficient mismatch.

references.title: Kleshchev, Sections 6.1-6.3 and 10.3
Perrin, Sections 4.2 and 12.3
